title.narrative: UNDP 2019-2023 Africa's Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction
UNDP 2019-2023 Resilience and Disaster Risk Reduction in Africa

description.narrative: The project "Strengthening capacities for disaster risk reduction and adaptation for Resilience in the Sahel Region: Fostering risk informed solutions for sustainable development main objective is that regional organizations (ECOWAS, CILSS/AGRHYMET, Peri Peri U & WASCAL, LCBC and AU) and national governments in the Sahel region have built capacities and have strengthened the operationalization of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction and the SDGs DRR targets and indicators. This will be conducted by institutionalized and domesticated risk-informed development planning, programming and investment for resilience building. The geographical focus of the project is Western Sahel (Mauritania, Mali, Senegal, Niger, Chad, Burkina Faso and Nigeria). This is expected to be achieved through 1) Increased capacity on tracking and monitoring progress on Sendai Framework and AU Program of Action implementation in the Sahel region through enhanced data collection, analysis and reporting system 2) Strengthened regional and multi-country regulatory, policy and budgetary frameworks for translating disaster and climate data into risk informed development 3) Enhanced regional recovery and resilience building processes that address underlying disaster and climate change risks and restore pathways to sustainable development in the Sahel Countries 4) Enhanced Regional Capacities for Urban Risk Management in Sahel and 5) Enhanced innovations and knowledge on risk informed development through Regional Dialogue and South- South exchange.

Insatsen syftar till att bygga kapacitet hos AU och regionala organisationer i Sahel (ECOWAS, CILSS/AGRHYMET och LCBC) att operationalisera Sendairamverket för katastrofriskreducering samt Globala målens indikatorer och mål för katastrofriskreducering.
Detta förväntas uppnås genom 1) Ökad kapacitet att följa och bevaka processerna kring Sendairamverket och AUs Program of Action Implementation genom förbättrad datainsamling, analys och system för rapportering; 2) Stärkta regionala ramverk för tillsyn, policy och budget för att möjliggöra användning av katastrofrisk- och klimatdata i utvecklingsplanering och budgetering; 3) Förstärkta regionala processer för återhämtning och klimatanpassning som adresserar faktorerna bakom klimatrelaterade katastrofer och återskapar möjliga vägar till hållbar utveckling i Sahelområdet; 4) Stärkt regional kapacitet för urban riskhantering i Västafrika; och 5) Innovation och ökad kunskap genom dialog och Syd-Syd samarbete.
Planerade aktiviteter inkluderar utvärderingar som tar hänsyn till genus och konflikt, fallstudier, framtagning av riktlinjer, utbildningar, workshops, Syd-Syd samarbete och inrättande av en regional informationsplattform. Projektet kommer implementeras av UNDP RSCA i partnerskap med ECOWAS och andra regionala organisationer (CILSS/AGRHYMET, LCBC, Peri Peri Uni & WASCAL, AUC, UNISDR och UN Women).

This contribution aims to build capacities of regional organizations in the Sahel (ECOWAS, CILSS/AGRHYMET and LCBC) and the African Union to strengthen the operationalization of the Sendai Framework for DRR, SDGs DRR targets and indicators.
This is expected to be achieved through 1) Increased capacity on tracking and monitoring progress on Sendai Framework and AU Program of Action implementation through enhanced data collection, analysis and reporting system; 2) Strengthened regional and multi-country regulatory, policy and budgetary frameworks for translating disaster and climate data into risk informed development planning and budgeting; 3) Enhanced regional recovery and resilience building processes that address underlying disaster and climate change risks and restore pathways to sustainable development in the Sahel Countries; 4) Enhanced Regional Capacities for Urban Risk Management in West Africa; and 5) Enhanced innovations and knowledge on risk informed development through Regional Dialogue and South-South exchange.
Planned activities include gender and conflict sensitive assessments, case studies, development or adoption of guidelines, trainings, workshops, south-south exchanges, and establishment of a regional information platform. The project will be directly implemented by UNDP RSCA in Partnership with ECOWAS and other regional organizations (CILSS/AGRHYMET, LCBC Peri Peri U & WASCAL), AUC, UNISDR and UN Women.

A second phase went operational back to back with the first phase of the intervention titled "Strengthening Capacities for Disaster Risk Reduction and Adaption for Resilience in the Sahel Region: fostering risk-informed solutions for Sustainable Development". The overall objective of the Project is to strengthen the policy and institutional capacities at the regional and national levels to understand the multidimensional risks that the region faces, and devise Due to the pandemic Sweden approved a budget reallocation of $1.4 million budget in May 2020, to strengthen regional capacities and enable national initiatives in the pandemic context. This laid the foundations for the development of the continental COVID19 Recovery Framework by the African Union Commission, driven by the recognition of intersecting risks and the imperative to safeguard sustainable development gains, particularly in the Sahel region. In 2021, the Project supported the comprehensive assessment and development by the AUC of the institutional and operational Framework for multi-hazard early warning and early action system for Africa (AMHEWAS).Financial and technical support for the implementation of AMHEWAS were provided by Italy along with UNDRR, the International Centre for Environmental Monitoring (CIMA) Research Foundation, UNDP, Sweden, and GIZ on behalf of Germany. Both continental frameworks, COVID19 Recovery and AMHEWAS were endorsed by AU Member States in February 2022, and launched by H.E. Filipe Jacinto Nyusi, President of Mozambique, and the African Unions Champion of Disaster Risk Management, during the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction in Maputo on 13 October 2022. The AUC and UNDP have jointly developed a project titled "Strengthening Capacities for Operationalization of AMHEWAS to Foster Anticipatory Action in Africa" designed to complement the Sahel Resilience Project (phase I and II). Two flagship studies have been conducted: A Comprehensive assessment of the socioeconomic impact of COVID19 and the role of disaster risk governance in the Western Sahel and Lake Chad Basin region in collaboration with ECOWAS and conducted by DataPop Alliance and ADE | Evidence for Better Policy and a study on the progress made by the seven project countries in the Sahel towards the implementation the AU Programme of Action for Sendai Framework for Disaster Reduction in collaboration with AUC. The last study has served as a concrete step towards fortifying the national capacities in setting their own disaster risk reduction strategies, among which Burkina Faso, Mali and Nigeria pioneered the process in 2023. AGRHYMET plays a pivotal role in managing and disseminating data and analytics on hydrology, food security, agroclimatology, and natural resource management across its 13 Member States, extending services to all ECOWAS Member States in its role as the Regional Climate Center. In 2021, a capacity assessment of AGRHYMET's potential to develop and host a regional risk information platform as well as to build and leverage partnerships at national, regional, and international levels according to its Member States directives was conducted. Based on the assessment, the Project supported the Center in addressing the critical human resources and equipment needs. The proposed cost-extension phase 2 to support AGRHYMETs cooperation with SMHI (the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrlogical Institute) is a step in the capacity development of AGRHYMET. AGRHYMET and UNDP (with support of its Country Offices) engaged some 351 stakeholders (70 women) in seven national workshops, spanning from 14 November 2022 to 30 August 2023, focusing on enhancing national disaster databases and disaster risk information management in Bamako (Mali), Abuja (Nigeria), Niamey (Niger), Manga (Burkina Faso), Etene (Chad), Nouakchott (Mauritania) and Saly (Senegal). In July 2023, AGRHYMET presented the prototype of the integrated risk information platform, aimed at standardizing data collection, aggregating regional data, and providing decision makers with timely information for disaster preparedness, and resilient recovery planning. The platform would initially focus on floods, droughts, food insecurity, and conflicts, also linking existing systems in these thematic areas developed and maintained through various project and initiatives. In addition to the resilience strategy for West Africa, UNDPs collaboration with the ECOWAS Commission within the partnership offered dedicated human resources including a project associate and a disaster recovery specialist, and will extend to a DRR specialist.
